newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela finds more dead children in quake ruins.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela finds more dead children in quake ruins.

text.p: The battered bodies of two young students were pulled on Sunday from the ruins of their school in eastern Venezuela, bringing the death toll from Wednesday's earthquake to 74.

The corpses of the two teenagers were found beneath the fallen masonry and broken desks of the Raimundo Martinez Centeno high school in Cariaco, 295 miles (470 km) east of Caracas, where dozens of children were crushed as they took end-of-term exams.

State Governor Ramon Martinez told reporters in the historic state capital Cumana, 40 miles (60 km) west, that 74 bodies had been retrieved from the debris left following the quake, which measured 6.9 on the Richter scale.
Despite intense rescue efforts -- including pumping oxygen into the ruins to keep those trapped alive -- rescuers have not found any survivors since Thursday morning.

Another seven bodies, including those of 5-year-old twins, were thought to be buried beneath the mound of twisted steel and concrete which was once an eight-story office building in Cumana, rescue officials said.
By early afternoon on Sunday cranes and bulldozers had removed what was left of the third floor of the building. The bodies were thought to be on the first floor.
More than 500 people were injured and another 500 families made homeless by Wednesday's quake -- Venezuela's deadliest for more than three decades.

The tiny agricultural town of Cariaco, where at least 40 children lost their lives, bore the brunt of the tremor. Two schools were flattened and about one quarter of the town's traditional mud-walled, straw roofed dwellings were damaged.
Martinez said 10 construction companies had been contracted to rebuild the town within a month. Portable toilets, mattresses, tents and power generators were due to arrive later on Sunday.
